headline: 1,593 hospitalized as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 184, with over 61,000 hospitalizations across Bangladesh.
details: Six people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a press release from the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
During the same period, 1,593 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
The distribution of new admissions includes 383 in the Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 171 in Dhaka North City Corporation, and 132 in Dhaka South City Corporation.
Other regions reported significant numbers: 290 in Khulna, 165 in Chattogram, 159 in Barishal, 137 in Rajshahi, 82 in Mymensingh, 65 in Rangpur, and 9 in Sylhet.
This brings the total number of dengue deaths this year to 184, with a total of 61,972 people hospitalized so far in 2024.

headline: 527 arrested as crude bomb blasts and arson attacks hit Dhaka
summary: Police have set up over 200 checkpoints across the capital to curb the wave of violence, including a recent blast at the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy.
details: A crude bomb exploded in front of the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy on Sunday between 1:15 PM and 2:00 PM. Assistant Commissioner of the Ramna division, Md. Mazharul Islam, confirmed the incident, though the perpetrators remain unknown.

Earlier on Sunday morning, a bus was set on fire near the Government College in the Pallabi area. Local residents extinguished the fire, which damaged the seats of the bus, before police began efforts to identify and arrest those involved.

The violence has escalated over the weekend, with three buses set on fire on Saturday and crude bomb blasts in the Jatrabari intersection and Shahid Faruk Sarani areas, leaving one auto-rickshaw driver injured.
On Friday, at least 13 crude bomb blasts occurred at nine different locations across the capital, including an arson attack on an empty bus in front of the Kafarul police station.

In response, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has implemented special security measures, establishing over 200 checkpoints at key points, flyovers, and entry points to the city to conduct searches.
According to a DMP press release, 527 people were arrested in the last 24 hours as part of regular operations. Additionally, 55 cases were filed during this period.

Police recovered various explosive materials, including an unexploded crude bomb, gunpowder, petrol, and nails, as well as significant quantities of narcotics including 54 kg of marijuana, over 4,000 Yaba pills, and heroin.
Authorities also seized two Yaba production machines, chemicals, and other materials used for drug manufacturing, alongside rescuing two victims.
